external_spec_note: The relation encodes a share-of-a-bounded-pot invariant (a lender's proportional principal claim cannot exceed the pool's total withdrawable liquidity) whose correctness rests on this contract's own pooled-credit-line share-accounting design (ERC1155 balanceOf representing a lender's minted share of pool _id) — not recoverable from generic language semantics or local comments alone.
case_notes: Two generic (Step-2) library facts are load-bearing but protocol-independent, so recorded here rather than counted: (1) SafeMath's .sub()/.mul()/.div() guarantee revert-on-underflow and floor division, which is what keeps _totalLiquidityWithdrawable non-negative on any non-reverting execution and makes the floor-scaling argument for the inequality hold; (2) balanceOf(_lender,_id) is a plain OpenZeppelin ERC1155Upgradeable getter that reduces exactly to reading state variable _balances[_id][_lender] (confirmed by the debug seed targeting `@StateVar _balances[_id][_lender]` rather than `@IReturn balanceOf(...)`) — an exact-formula inlining of a generic, protocol-independent one-line getter.
extraction_note: Judgment call: POOLED_CREDIT_LINE.getPrincipal(_id) (external cross-contract call feeding _totalLiquidityWithdrawable) is debug-seeded via `@IReturn ... = [0,0]` but was excluded from Additional functions/contracts and from context_breadth. Applying the Step-1 load-bearing test literally: _principalWithdrawable = _totalLiquidityWithdrawable * balanceOf(_lender,_id) / _borrowedTokens is <= _totalLiquidityWithdrawable whenever balanceOf(_lender,_id) <= _borrowedTokens and _totalLiquidityWithdrawable >= 0 (guaranteed by SafeMath.sub not reverting) -- true for ANY value getPrincipal(_id) returns that doesn't cause a revert. So the annotated inequality's validity does not actually depend on getPrincipal's specific returned value; the debug seed exists to fix a concrete number for an RQ1-B engine run, not because the R1-3 relation's own derivation needs it.
